keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Mauritius row begins in 1969 but 'independence was proclaimed on 12 March 1968'.

2,480 km2 against the infobox 2,040 km2 (ratio 1.22, within the factor of two; the infobox total covers the island and the outliers, so Cliopatria's figure is a cell-rounded outline of the main island only, bbox 57.18-57.70E, 19.96-20.54S). Rodrigues, Agaléga and St. Brandon belong to the Republic ('The Republic of Mauritius comprises Mauritius Island and several outlying islands') but resolve to 0 grid cells, so nothing is added. The Chagos Archipelago, split away in 1965, is not in the shape.

Same outline (2,480 km2). The October 2024 UK-Mauritius statement says sovereignty over the Chagos Archipelago 'was to have' been transferred, the treaty was signed in May 2025 and was awaiting ratification: no land is added in 2024.

region.text: Mauritius Island with Rodrigues, Agaléga and St. Brandon

ledger.note: 12 March 1968: Mauritius becomes independent from the United Kingdom. 'independence was proclaimed on 12 March 1968.' The Republic 'comprises Mauritius Island and several outlying islands'; the Chagos Archipelago had been split away in 1965 and formed the British Indian Ocean Territory (established 8 November 1965).
12 March 1992: Mauritius is proclaimed a republic. 'On 12 March 1992, Mauritius was proclaimed a republic within the Commonwealth of Nations.' The state and its land continue.

certainty.note: An island state: coastlines are the border. The exceptions are claims: Mauritius claims Tromelin Island, 'registered as a part of France' (a 2010 co-management treaty 'has not been ratified'), and the Chagos Archipelago until the 2024 agreement.

notes: One page only (budget 1-2 for 2 shapes). NOT SETTLED: (1) Chagos: the page dates the 1965 detachment (BIOT established 8 November 1965, before the state), the ICJ opinion (February 2019) and General Assembly vote (May 2019), the October 2024 joint statement and the May 2025 signing, with no days; no contest is drawn (removed by review af-08-l, 2026-10-24): a sovereignty dispute pursued in the ICJ and the UN General Assembly, not on the ground, like Tromelin in (3); the claim is in certainty. The status after 2024 (ratification, a 2026 transfer is tagged [citation needed] on the page) belongs to a later update: a gain from the UK once the treaty takes effect. (2) Rodrigues became 'an autonomous entity within the republic' in 2002 (no border change); Agaléga and St. Brandon are outlying islands with no sovereignty claim recorded. (3) Tromelin Island: Mauritius claims it, France holds it; the page dates a 1959 British statement and the 2010 co-management treaty; no contest event is written because no border is contested on the ground. (4) The 1968 keyframe is new: Cliopatria's row begins 1969. (5) Cliopatria has no row for the Mauritius colony before independence (its 'French India' row 1673-1847 reaches Mauritius per data/polities.csv, and the British Colonial Empire shapes have no neighbour relation with the island from 1969); the colony's earlier history is for another dossier. No ruler strip and no wars: the page opened lists no list of heads of state.
